identity.title: ALMA and VLA reveal the lukewarm chromospheres of the nearby red supergiants Antares and Betelgeuse

paper_type_evidence.quote: We first present spatially resolved ALMA and VLA continuum observations of the early-M red supergiant Antares to search for the presence of a chromosphere at radio wavelengths.

evidence.quote: it is possible that Antares is the nearest RSG ($d=170^{+35}_{-25}\,$pc, (cite: van_Leeuwen_2007))
it is possible that Antares is the nearest RSG ($d=170^{+35}_{-25}\,$pc, (cite: van_Leeuwen_2007))

question.value: Does the red supergiant Antares have a chromosphere detectable at radio wavelengths, and what are its temperature structure and spectral index from ALMA band 8 to VLA S band?

evidence.quote: We first present spatially resolved ALMA and VLA continuum observations of the early-M red supergiant Antares to search for the presence of a chromosphere at radio wavelengths.
(project code: 2016.1.00234.S, PI: Eamon O’Gorman)

bands.value: ALMA bands 3, 4, 7, 8; VLA S, C, X, Ku, K, Ka, Q

evidence.quote: Antares was observed with ALMA in four unique continuum bands (bands 3, 4, 7, and 8) between July and October 2017

continuum_bandwidth.value: 7.5 GHz effective bandwidth over four spectral windows per ALMA band

evidence.quote: with 7.5 GHz effective bandwidth spread over four spectral windows in each of the bands

evidence.quote: with only between 3 and 5 minutes spent on the target in each track

method.value: Model the ionized region with CLEAN, Fourier transform with FT, subtract with UVSUB at S, C, X bands

evidence.quote: Finally, the UVSUB task was used to subtract this model from the actual visibilities to leave a dataset containing only the visibilities of Antares.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit size, shape and flux in uv-plane

method.value: Fit uniform-intensity circular disks (VLA) and elliptical disks (ALMA) with spectral index free to visibilities

evidence.loc: 3.1 Size and shape of the Antares atmosphere
evidence.quote: Uniform-intensity elliptical disk models in which the flux density depended on frequency (i.e., a spectral index) were found to fit all of the four ALMA datasets best.

validation.value: Residual images show no substantial residuals

evidence.loc: 3.1 Size and shape of the Antares atmosphere
evidence.quote: because no substantial residuals are detected in any of the residual images, we are confident that our model represents the data well

method.value: Brightness temperature from flux and diameter equals local gas temperature where optical depth ~1; plotted against radius

evidence.quote: the brightness temperature is just the local gas temperature where the optical depth is near unity, averaged across the stellar disk

assumptions.value: Optically thick thermal emission; photospheric diameter 37.38 mas

evidence.quote: where the diameter of the optical photosphere is 37.38 mas (cite: ohnaka_2013)

method.value: Estimate H- opacity of MOLsphere from CO column density at 2000 K in chemical equilibrium

findings_qualitative.value: ALMA atmosphere is elongated (15% flattening) at similar position angle in all four bands

evidence.quote: All four ALMA measurements show that the shape of the atmosphere is elongated, with a flattening of 15% at a similar position angle.

claims.hypothesis: Antares has a chromospheric temperature rise detectable at radio wavelengths
claims.experiment: Multi-frequency ALMA+VLA uv-plane disk fits and brightness temperatures
claims.result: Tb rises from 2682 K at 1.35 R* to 3777 K at ~2.5 R*, then falls to 1647 K

evidence.quote: The rise in gas temperature between 1.35 $R_{\star}$ and $\sim$2.5 $R_{\star}$ is evidence for a chromospheric temperature rise

claims.hypothesis: Lukewarm temperature could be an average of hot and cool MOLsphere gas
claims.experiment: Optical depth of MOLsphere with H- opacity

evidence.quote: We show that the Antares MOLsphere is transparent at our observed wavelengths

claims.result: Radio-temperature model underpredicts FUV; hot photoionization component needed
claims.finding: Hot (>7000 K) component with small filling factor exists

evidence.quote: an additional hot (i.e., $>7000\,$K) chromospheric photoionization component with a much smaller filling factor must also exist

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Term 'radio photosphere' deemed unnecessary for RSGs since their radio properties differ from AGB stars

evidence.loc: 4.5 RSGs versus AGB stars at radio wavelengths
evidence.quote: the inclusion of the term *radio photosphere* is unnecessary

limitations_admitted.value: Beams comparable to stellar size, so properties derived from visibilities; small-scale structure needs higher resolution

evidence.quote: ALMA continuum data with higher spatial resolution are required to detect such features

referee_caveats_inferred: Model-dependent uniform disk fits give very small formal errors
Brightness temperature equals gas temperature assumes tau~1 and optically thick
